\">\u003cfigcaption>Figure · page 39\u003c/figcaption>\u003c/figure>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 40\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Follow-up surveillance endoscopy is then continued periodically because varices may recur  over time.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Non-Selective Beta Blockers\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Long-term pharmacological prevention includes:Propranolol, Nadolol, Carvedilol.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">These agents reduce portal pressure through: β1 blockade → reduced cardiac output, β2\u003cbr>blockade → splanchnic vasoconstriction.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">The result is: reduced portal venous inflow, reduced variceal wall tension, and reduced risk of  rupture.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">According to hepatology guidelines: Combination therapy using: EVL plus beta blockers\u003cbr>provides better prevention than either therapy alone. Carvedilol may produce greater portal\u003cbr>pressure reduction because it also has: Alpha-1 blocking activity leading to intrahepatic\u003cbr>vasodilation.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">However, excessive beta blockade may cause:\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">•  hypotension,   •  renal hypoperfusion,   •  fatigue,   •  and worsening refractory ascites in advanced cirrhosis.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Therefore dose titration and monitoring are essential. Optimization of Chronic Liver\u003cbr>Disease Long-term prevention also requires treatment of the: Underlying liver disease\u003cbr>because portal hypertension and varices are consequences of chronic hepatic injury.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Alcohol Cessation\u003c/h4>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Prevention of Hepatic Encephalopathy\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Lactulose decreases ammonia absorption by acidifying colonic contents, trapping ammonia\u003cbr>as ammonium, and increasing fecal nitrogen excretion.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Management of Ascites and Portal Hypertension\u003c/p>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 41\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Long-Term Prevention in Non-Variceal Bleeding\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Peptic ulcer disease\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">H. pylori Eradication\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Avoidance of NSAIDs\u003c/p>\u003cfigure class=\"note-figure\">\u003cimg loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Illustration associated with page 41\" src=\"data:image/webp;base64,\">\u003cfigcaption>Figure · page 41\u003c/figcaption>\u003c/figure>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 42\u003c/div>\u003cfigure class=\"note-figure\">\u003cimg loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Illustration associated with page 42\" src=\"data:image/webp;base64,\">\u003cfigcaption>Figure · page 42\u003c/figcaption>\u003c/figure>\u003cfigure class=\"note-figure\">\u003cimg loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Illustration associated with page 42\" src=\"data:image/webp;base64,
